subject: Next steps — EU dataflow matrix & connectivity check (Aurora Health)
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Garth Lowe <garth.lowe@aurorahealth.com>, Aurora Health Procurement <procurement@aurorahealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Next steps — EU dataflow matrix & connectivity check (Aurora Health)

Hi Garth / team,

Thanks again for the call earlier — good alignment on scope. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth: 

Summary of pain & goals
- Data residency: all PHI must remain in EU region; no logs or backups stored outside EU.
- Regulatory driver: Aurora’s audit requires an air-gapped analytics lane for some workloads and strict key management.
- Connectivity: environment is behind a private VPC with no general outbound internet (egress-only via approved proxy), and only allowlisted fixed IPs are permitted for vendor endpoints.
- Timeline: POC targeted in Q3 (internal deadline: readiness by mid-August).

What we agreed we need next
1) Network/dataflow matrix from Aurora (we need VPC/subnet ranges, NAT/proxy architecture, egress controls).
2) Confirmation on whether a reverse-proxy/whitelisted outbound is acceptable for model-serving traffic, or if an entirely offline bundle is required.
3) KMS/HSM requirements and whether Aurora will manage keys (customer-managed) or require Redwood to integrate with their HSM.
4) SOC 2 / pen-test evidence for initial security review (you mentioned a summary pack on the call).

Attachments I’m sharing now (attached to this thread):
- redwood-private-sku.pdf (initial hosting options + network requirements)
- network-checklist-template.xlsx (editable checklist to fill in VPC details)

Proposed next steps / owners
- Garth: share the completed network-checklist-template + SOC2 summary by end of this week.
- Procurement: confirm procurement timeline and required SOW/PO template.
- Karthik (cc’d): schedule a technical deep-dive to validate endpoints / allowlisting approach.

Suggested times for a 60-minute technical workshop:
- Wed 26 May, 10:00-11:00 CET
- Thu 27 May, 14:00-15:00 CET

If those don’t work I’ll send a few more slots.

Thanks — I’ll queue the internal SOW template and a short diagram illustrating the two hosting patterns we discussed (1: VPC-with-proxy egress; 2: hermetic-onprem bundle).

Best,

Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192

Attachments: redwood-private-sku.pdf, network-checklist-template.xlsx
From: Garth Lowe <garth.lowe@aurorahealth.com>

Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 20:17:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Next steps — EU dataflow matrix & connectivity check (Aurora Health)

Ben — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming a few clarifications from our side: 

- Data residency: correct — primary requirement is EU-only storage. Backups must be stored in the EU and retention policies enforced by Aurora.
- Egress model: our security team prefers egress through our managed proxy (allowlist specific vendor IPs). Full air-gap for the analytics lane is desired for PHI processing, but we are open to a hybrid approach for non-PHI inference if you can guarantee no cross-region telemetry.
- Keys: Aurora will require customer-managed keys in our HSM for PHI-related workloads. Any vendor-managed key option needs explicit justification and additional attestation.
- Evidence: attaching SOC2 summary + network ACL export for initial triage (aurora-soc2-summary.pdf, aurora-network-acls.xlsx). We will not share full penetration test reports at this stage, but can provide a redacted executive summary under NDA.

Procurement note: procurement@aurorahealth.com — we will need a SOW and an estimated monthly committed spend for the POC to route to finance. Our procurement timeline target is two weeks to review the SOW.

We can do Wed 26 May 10:00 CET — I’ll accept a calendar invite. Karthik, please include a short list of the IPs your endpoints will use so our network team can start allowlisting ahead of the call.

Garth Lowe
Director, IT Security | Aurora Health
garth.lowe@aurorahealth.com | +44 20 7946 0821

Subject: Re: Next steps — EU dataflow matrix & connectivity check (Aurora Health)

Thanks Garth — Karthik (solutions engineering) here. Short technical follow-up and commitments from our side: 

1) I attached a pre-filled network-checklist (same template Ben linked) and a one-page connectivity diagram for the two hosting patterns we discussed. That will help your network team map expected flows and NAT/route behavior.
2) For the allowlisting ask: Redwood can provide a set of static egress IPs for dedicated pools; we will also supply an outbound proxy FQDN if you prefer DNS-based allowlisting. I will list the IPs on the follow-up.
3) KMS/HSM: we support customer-managed keys via standard KMIP-compatible HSMs or AWS KMS with external key control. For the POC, we recommend using your HSM for PHI workloads; we can provide the integration checklist.
4) Telemetry & logs: we can redact or truncate logs for PII before forwarding; for auditability we can stream encrypted logs into your S3 in EU with your own SSE-KMS.

Action items (who/when)
- Aurora: return completed network-checklist-template.xlsx + confirm whether the analytics lane must be fully air-gapped (deadline: Tue 25 May EOD).
- Ben / Marissa: prepare preliminary SOW draft and cost estimate for the POC (Ben will lead, Marissa will review).
- Karthik: share static IP list + integration checklist by Mon 24 May EOD.

I’ll send the calendar invite for Wed 26 May 10:00 CET and include a short pre-read. Looking forward to the workshop.

Cheers,

Karthik Iyer
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
